warns: verdict tier 0 < target 2: not best on nominal: ours 1.993 vs ZV input shaping 1.89

agent_summary: In a small CPU simulation with a reduced-order two-mode nonlinear slosh model, MPC with a learned slosh predictor was spill-free and 7% faster than fitted-pendulum MPC on the nominal liquid, but slower than a fitted two-mode spring-mass model and open-loop ZV input shaping. On held-out liquids with pushes the learned model gave the better time-spill trade-off at equal transport time (though the slower pendulum spilled less at tuned margins), the advantage vanished for a single linear mode, and force/torque sensing was not better than a height probe.
